title: How to Choose an Electric Kettle (and the Right Tea Temperature)
h1: How to Choose an Electric Kettle
metaDescription: Gooseneck or standard, variable temperature or simple boil? How to choose an electric kettle, with a tea temperature chart.
lede: The right kettle depends on what you make with the water. Here is what matters, and what you can safely ignore.

p: Boiling water can make delicate teas taste bitter. If you drink green, white or oolong tea, a variable-temperature kettle is worth it. If you mainly drink black tea or instant coffee, a basic kettle is enough.
These are widely used starting points; follow the instructions on your tea if they differ.
list: Black and herbal tea: about 200 to 212°F (93 to 100°C)

p: A gooseneck spout gives a slow, precise stream for pour-over coffee. A standard spout pours faster and is better for filling mugs, teapots and pans.
Look for these on any kettle:
list: Automatic shut-off when the water boils
A cordless base that lets you lift the kettle off
A clear water-level window or markings

p: Around 1.7 liters suits most households. Smaller gooseneck kettles (under 1 liter) are designed for one or two cups of coffee or tea at a time.

faqs.q: How often should I descale a kettle?
faqs.a: Every few weeks to every few months, depending on how hard your water is. Follow the manufacturer's instructions for the descaling method.

faqs.q: Is it safe to leave water in a kettle?
faqs.a: It's generally fine for short periods, but emptying and refilling with fresh water gives better-tasting drinks and slows limescale build-up.
